Title: Create, sign, change, cancel and refill medication order
Test Case Description: Clinician completes the medication lifecycle for a synthetic patient.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Clinician is authenticated with TOTP.
2. Synthetic patient and medication catalog exist.
Test Steps:
1. Open patient record.
2. Create a valid order and sign it.
3. Change dose and save.
4. Cancel the order.
5. Create a refill for the eligible order.
Test Data: drug=amoxicillin; dose=500 mg; route=oral; frequency=BID; synthetic patient
Expected Result:
1. Each valid action succeeds.
2. Current status and fields are stored on the patient record.
3. Prior versions remain visible in immutable history.

Title: Required medication fields are enforced
Test Case Description: Reject an order missing each required clinical field.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Clinician is authenticated.
2. Patient record is open.
Test Steps:
1. Submit an order with one required field omitted.
2. Repeat for drug, dose, route, frequency and patient.
Expected Result:
1. Order is not signed or persisted.
2. Field-specific validation identifies the missing value.

Title: Medication lifecycle invalid transition
Test Case Description: Prevent refill or change after a terminal cancellation.
Pre-Conditions: 1. A medication order is cancelled.
Test Steps:
1. Attempt to refill the cancelled order.
2. Attempt to edit the cancelled order.
Expected Result:
1. Action is rejected without mutation.
2. Clear message explains the terminal-state restriction.

Title: Interaction alert blocks or permits by configured threshold
Test Case Description: Check drug-drug and drug-allergy rules before signing.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Clinician is entering an order.
2. Active medication/allergy and seeded interaction rule exist.
3. Admin threshold is configured.
Test Steps:
1. Enter a conflicting drug.
2. Observe alert before signing.
3. Try sign at blocking severity.
4. Repeat with a severity below configured threshold.
Expected Result:
1. Alert names the interaction and severity before signing.
2. Blocking severity prevents sign.
3. Permitted severity requires explicit acknowledgement and then signs.

Title: Interaction table and threshold boundary validation
Test Case Description: Verify seeded rules and allowed administrator threshold range.
Pre-Conditions: 1. Administrator is authenticated.
Test Steps:
1. Set threshold to minimum allowed value.
2. Set threshold to maximum allowed value.
3. Submit below-minimum and above-maximum values.
4. Check a known seeded pair.
Expected Result:
1. Boundary values save.
2. Out-of-range values are rejected with no change.
3. Known rule returns expected severity.

Title: Severity floors and critical interaction blocking
Test Case Description: Verify alert severities use only LOW, MODERATE and HIGH, and critical safety findings always block signing.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Clinician is entering orders.
2. Seeded rules cover LOW, MODERATE, HIGH and critical cases.
Test Steps:
1. Trigger each severity.
2. Attempt to sign without acknowledgement and with acknowledgement.
3. Attempt to change a critical rule through threshold configuration.
Expected Result:
1. Only LOW, MODERATE and HIGH are displayed/stored.
2. Critical findings always block signing regardless of configured threshold.
3. Critical severity cannot be lowered or bypassed.

Title: Demographics coded fields and date rules
Test Case Description: Create and edit all P0 demographic fields with coded values.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Clinician has patient edit permission.
2. Standard public terminology subsets are loaded.
Test Steps:
1. Enter race, ethnicity, preferred language, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity from code lists.
2. Enter date of birth and optional date of death.
3. Save and reopen.
Test Data: synthetic coded values; DOB=1980-01-01; death date=2020-01-01
Expected Result:
1. All values persist and display using codes/labels, not disallowed free text.
2. Dates are stored accurately.

Title: Demographics invalid code and date validation
Test Case Description: Reject unknown terminology codes and impossible dates.
Pre-Conditions: 1. Patient edit form is open.
Test Steps:
1. Submit an unknown code.
2. Submit death date before birth date.
3. Submit malformed date.
Expected Result:
1. No invalid value persists.
2. Inline errors identify code/date problems.

Title: Single-patient JSON export with dictionary
Test Case Description: Authorized user exports one synthetic patient in JSON.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Authorized clinician or patient is authenticated with TOTP.
2. Patient has demographics, medications, allergies and problems.
Test Steps:
1. Start export for exactly one patient.
2. Download JSON and data dictionary.
3. Parse JSON and inspect metadata.
Expected Result:
1. Export contains only selected patient data.
2. JSON is machine-readable and includes the data dictionary.
3. Export action is audited.

Title: Export authorization and fifteen-minute expiry
Test Case Description: Verify exports are restricted and links expire after 15 minutes.
Pre-Conditions:
1. A valid export exists.
2. A user without patient authorization is available.
Test Steps:
1. Request another patient export without authorization.
2. Access a valid export before 15 minutes.
3. Access the same link at 15 minutes plus one second.
Expected Result:
1. Unauthorized request is denied.
2. Valid link works within 15 minutes.
3. Expired link is unusable and returns an informative error.

Title: Human-readable and machine-readable patient download
Test Case Description: Patient views and downloads their own record in JSON and PDF.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Patient is authenticated with TOTP.
2. Own record has synthetic data.
Test Steps:
1. Open record.
2. Download JSON.
3. Download PDF.
4. Open both files.
Expected Result:
1. Record is viewable.
2. Both downloads are readable and contain only the patient record.
3. Download actions are audited.

Title: PDF export hash is exact SHA256
Test Case Description: Verify JSON/PDF export integrity metadata.
Pre-Conditions: 1. An authorized export has completed.
Test Steps:
1. Compute SHA256 over each downloaded file bytes.
2. Compare with the supplied hash.
3. Alter one byte and verify mismatch.
Expected Result:
1. Supplied hash exactly matches SHA-256 for each file.
2. Any byte alteration is detected.

Title: FHIR six-resource read and search success
Test Case Description: Read and search the six P0 FHIR resources.
Pre-Conditions:
1. FHIR client has valid access token and consent.
2. Seeded synthetic data includes all six resources.
Test Steps:
1. GET each resource by id.
2. Search each resource with supported parameters.
3. Validate response content type and FHIR metadata.
Test Data: Patient; MedicationRequest; AllergyIntolerance; Condition; Observation; Device
Expected Result:
1. Each read/search returns valid FHIR R4 data.
2. Device is readable and explicitly read-only.
3. No unsupported write is implied.

Title: FHIR malformed request, failure and timeout handling
Test Case Description: Verify deterministic API responses for bad payload, unavailable dependency and timeout.
Pre-Conditions: 1. FHIR endpoint is reachable.
Test Steps:
1. Send malformed JSON where applicable.
2. Request an unknown resource/id.
3. Simulate upstream/database timeout.
4. Inspect status, FHIR error shape and logs.
Expected Result:
1. Malformed input returns 4xx with safe OperationOutcome.
2. Missing resource returns expected not-found response.
3. Timeout returns controlled 5xx/timeout response without partial data.
4. No secrets or EHI appear in client error.

Title: SMART app registration and explicit-consent standalone launch
Test Case Description: Register a developer app and complete standalone OAuth with explicit consent.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Public demo terminology/subsets and developer portal are available.
2. Developer has a valid synthetic account.
Test Steps:
1. Register app with valid redirect URI and scopes.
2. Start standalone authorization.
3. Review consent screen.
4. Approve and exchange code for tokens.
5. Call permitted FHIR read.
Expected Result:
1. Registration is self-service/free.
2. Consent explicitly names app, patient context and scopes.
3. Tokens are issued only after approval.
4. Permitted read succeeds.

Title: SMART EHR launch, refresh and consent denial
Test Case Description: Cover EHR launch and denied/expired OAuth paths.
Pre-Conditions:
1. Registered app exists.
2. Synthetic clinician session exists for EHR launch.
Test Steps:
1. Start EHR launch from clinician context.
2. Deny consent.
3. Repeat approval, let access token expire, use refresh token.
4. Revoke/expire refresh token and retry.
Test Data: launch=EHR; expired access token; revoked refresh token
Expected Result:
1. EHR context is bounded to authorized patient.
2. Denial yields no token and no data.
3. Valid refresh obtains a new access token.
4. Invalid refresh is rejected and audited.

Title: Role access matrix and patient self-only restriction
Test Case Description: Verify clinician, patient and administrator permissions.
Expected Result: Clinician can access demo patients; patient only own record; admin manages approved settings; denied actions are safely handled.

Title: Unauthenticated, injection and session-expiry denial
Test Case Description: Ensure access is denied before identity verification and after session expiry.
Expected Result: Unauthenticated calls return 401; inputs are treated as data; expired session requires re-authentication.

Title: Mandatory TOTP enrollment and verification
Test Case Description: Require TOTP for every role and reject invalid/replayed codes.
Expected Result: Password-only login cannot establish a session; valid TOTP establishes session; invalid codes fail safely.

Title: Salted one-way credential storage
Test Case Description: Verify credentials are never stored plaintext and salts/work factor are used.
Expected Result: Stored values are salted one-way hashes with modern work factor; equal passwords differ.

Title: Configurable inactivity timeout and re-authentication
Test Case Description: End idle sessions at configured timeout.
Expected Result: Pre-timeout request works; post-timeout request is denied and session invalidated; re-authentication restores access.

Title: Append-only audit hash chain and verification
Test Case Description: Verify every auditable event is chained and tampering is detected.
Expected Result: Each event contains actor, timestamp, patient, resource, action, previous hash and hash; tampering fails verification.

Title: Audit report filters sorting and structured-log separation
Test Case Description: Admin reviews audit events using all report filters and confirms app logs are separate.
Expected Result: Filters and sorting are deterministic; audit records are distinct from structured application logs.

Title: Browser EHI storage prohibition
Test Case Description: Verify no EHI is persisted in browser storage by default.
Expected Result: No EHI is stored in browser storage by default; sign-out removes transient session material.

Title: Exact SHA256 on API transmission
Test Case Description: Verify each FHIR transmission carries a verifiable exact SHA-256 or stronger hash.
Expected Result: Digest matches exact response bytes and detects alteration.

Title: TLS 1.2 minimum and local certificate behavior
Test Case Description: Ensure local demo traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher.
Expected Result: TLS 1.2+ succeeds; older protocols fail; protected traffic is not plaintext.

Title: Django DRF PostgreSQL React TypeScript integration
Test Case Description: Verify the approved stack interoperates across a representative read and write flow.
Expected Result: Client, API and database exchange data through typed-safe responses with PostgreSQL persistence.

Title: Synthetic-only data and public demo terminology subsets
Test Case Description: Prevent real EHI and verify approved public terminology subsets are used.
Expected Result: Fixtures and outputs are synthetic only; real-data import is rejected or isolated.

Title: Performance under 500ms for typical page and FHIR read
Test Case Description: Measure typical demo page and FHIR read latency.
Expected Result: Typical page and FHIR read responses are under 500 ms.

Title: Empty, loading and no-results states are safe
Test Case Description: Verify empty patient search, loading state and no FHIR search results.
Expected Result: Empty input is safe; loading is visible; no-results is clear and reveals no data.

Title: Concurrent medication edits preserve immutable history
Test Case Description: Ensure concurrent edits do not silently overwrite clinical history.
Expected Result: One update accepted by policy; stale update conflicts or safely merges; prior version is retained.

Title: Partial export failure rolls back incomplete artifact
Test Case Description: Ensure a failed export leaves no misleading partial download or audit success.
Expected Result: No incomplete artifact is successful; state cleans up consistently; retry can succeed.

Title: Regression: core flow remains audited after correction
Test Case Description: Re-run the end-to-end clinician and patient flows after updates.
Expected Result: Core flow succeeds; correction preserves history; patient scope and audit remain valid.

Title: Alternate medication search by coded identifier
Test Case Description: Use an alternate supported lookup path before ordering.
Expected Result: Lookup returns same medication identity; selection does not alter unrelated data.

Title: API bad payload does not partially persist medication
Test Case Description: Reject malformed DRF medication payload atomically.
Expected Result: API returns validation 4xx; no medication or partial version persists.

Title: Admin threshold permission denied to non-admin
Test Case Description: Ensure only administrators can alter interaction severity thresholds.
Expected Result: Non-admin updates are denied; admin can update within allowed range.

Title: FHIR Device is seeded read-only
Test Case Description: Verify seeded Device is available but cannot be changed through P0 API.
Expected Result: Read/search return seeded Device; writes are rejected.

Title: Security error messages do not disclose account or patient existence
Test Case Description: Check uniform safe messages for unauthorized login, patient lookup and OAuth denial.
Expected Result: Messages do not reveal whether an account/patient exists or expose EHI/secrets.

Title: Database/API outage returns controlled rollback
Test Case Description: Verify a medication save and audit write do not diverge during database/API failure.
Expected Result: Operation reports failure; record and audit remain consistent; retry is safe.

Title: Structured auth events recursively redact sensitive fields
Test Case Description: Emit allowlisted operational events with nested sensitive values supplied by an auth failure.
Expected Result: Events retain approved outcome metadata while recursively denying or redacting passwords OTP secrets tokens cookies PII clinical payloads and connection strings.

Title: Correlation identifier is sanitized or generated at backend boundary
Test Case Description: Send valid and malformed correlation headers through an auth request.
Expected Result: A safe correlation identifier is present in every backend event and response header without accepting attacker-controlled content.

Title: TOTP enrollment emits entry success and failure events
Test Case Description: Perform enrollment and enrollment verification with valid and invalid inputs.
Expected Result: Each enrollment operation emits explicit entry and success or failure events with correlation context and no secret or OTP values.

Title: Authentication exceptions preserve safe exception context
Test Case Description: Force an external authentication failure and inspect the emitted operational event.
Expected Result: Failure event contains safe exception classification and correlation context while omitting request bodies credentials and traceback payloads.

Title: Frontend auth logger records classified outcomes
Test Case Description: Invoke the browser authentication request against successful and failed HTTP responses.
Expected Result: Injected logger receives entry and sanitized exit or failure records including HTTP classification duration and correlation identifier without bodies or secrets.

Title: External authentication call has entry exit and failure observability
Test Case Description: Exercise the Django external authentication boundary for success and failure.
Expected Result: Backend records call entry and exit or failure without logging credentials response bodies or tokens.

Title: Correlation context is isolated between sequential requests
Test Case Description: Dispatch sequential requests including an exception and inspect correlation context after each request.
Expected Result: Each request receives only its own correlation identifier; context is reset after normal and exceptional dispatch.

Title: Frontend auth HTTP status is logged with its class
Test Case Description: Invoke browser authentication against a failed HTTP response and inspect the injected logger record.
Expected Result: Response-backed auth records contain the exact numeric HTTP status and sanitized 3xx/4xx/5xx class without response bodies.
src/auth.test.ts::TC-EHR-0047 frontend auth logs exact response status

Title: Tracer exception metadata is bounded and sanitized
Test Case Description: Raise an exception through a traced function with a cause chain and inspect the trace event.
Expected Result: Trace exception records contain safe class/code, bounded cause metadata, and controlled stack locations without messages or arguments; the exception is re-raised.

Title: Medication draft required fields and prescriber
Test Case Description: Clinician submits a medication draft with all required fields and rejects incomplete payloads.
Pre-Conditions: Clinician and synthetic patient exist.
Test Steps: Submit valid and one-field-missing drafts.
Test Data: coded medication; positive dose and quantity; route; frequency; start date; indication; clinician prescriber
Expected Result: Valid draft persists; invalid payload is rejected without medication or audit mutation.

Title: Medication immutable version history
Test Case Description: Changing an order appends a version and supersedes the prior version.
Pre-Conditions: A medication draft exists.
Test Steps: Change dose then retrieve history.
Expected Result: Prior version remains unchanged and both versions are retrievable.

Title: Medication cancellation and refill transitions
Test Case Description: Cancellation is terminal and refill creates a new draft only when eligible.
Pre-Conditions: A medication order with refills exists.
Test Steps: Cancel or refill then attempt an invalid terminal transition.
Expected Result: Cancel is terminal; cancelled orders cannot change or refill; refill never signs or activates unsafely.

Title: Medication authorization and atomic audit
Test Case Description: Only clinicians mutate and every successful mutation has one atomic audit event.
Pre-Conditions: Clinician patient and admin sessions exist.
Test Steps: Attempt mutations by each role and simulate audit failure.
Expected Result: Unauthorized mutations are rejected; failed mutation and audit leave no partial state.

Title: Medication clinician form safe states
Test Case Description: Clinician form exposes validation loading error empty and explicit pre-sign states.
Pre-Conditions: Clinician opens a patient record.
Test Steps: Load submit invalid/valid data and inspect history.
Expected Result: States are clear; signing and interaction rules are deferred to Ticket05.
